- **Non-Watertight Meshes:** The method depends on having one back face for every front face.
- **Degenerate Intersections:** Triangles parallel to the slice or lying exactly on the slice plane may produce zero or infinite intersections.
- **Offset Direction Ambiguity:** If the triangle normal is perpendicular to the slice plane, the projection is zero.
In this case, the offset direction is undefined.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N_{tri} \cdot N_{slices})$, where $N_{tri}$ is the number of triangles and $N_{slices}$ is the number of grid slices.
Each triangle is processed once per slice.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N_x \cdot N_y \cdot N_z)$ for the 3D texture.
Performance depends on mesh complexity and grid resolution.
- **Strengths:** Directly computes velocity field; handles moving obstacles efficiently; suitable for real-time simulation.
- **Limitations:** Requires watertight meshes; sensitive to mesh quality and slice alignment; additive blending may require normalization if multiple layers contribute.
Velocity Voxelization was introduced in the context of real-time 3D fluid simulation, specifically for coupling rigid body dynamics with fluid solvers.
The method leverages GPU geometry shaders to efficiently compute boundary velocities for voxel-based fluid solvers.
